userStories.title: Spec Diff View for Version Comparison
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to compare two versions of a generated spec side-by-side so I can understand what changed between regenerations and make informed approval decisions.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/specs/:specId/versions returns an array of all previously generated versions for that spec slug with timestamps
GET /api/specs/:specId/diff?v1={version1}&v2={version2} returns a structured diff showing added, removed, and modified stories and acceptance criteria
The diff output includes per-story change type (added | removed | modified | unchanged) and per-field deltas for modified stories
Rejected specs are retained as versions (not deleted) so they appear in the version history with rejection reason attached

userStories.title: Spec Template Library with Reusable Patterns
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to save successful spec structures as templates so I can reuse proven patterns across projects without rewriting briefs from scratch.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/templates creates a template from an approved spec, extracting the brief, story structure, and direction stack layers used
GET /api/templates lists all templates with name, description, source spec ID, story count, and created_at
POST /api/specs/generate accepts an optional templateId parameter that pre-populates the generation prompt with the template's structure as a reference pattern
Templates are workspace-agnostic and available across all workspaces
DELETE /api/templates/:id removes a template and returns 204

userStories.title: Multi-Model Support for Spec Generation
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to choose which LLM model generates my specs so I can compare output quality across models and optimize for cost or capability.
acceptanceCriteria: The /api/specs/generate endpoint accepts an optional 'model' parameter supporting at least 'claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929', 'claude-opus-4-6', and 'claude-haiku-4-5-20251001'
The model used is recorded in the spec metadata and displayed in the review queue
Default model is configurable per workspace via PUT /api/direction with a new 'preferred_model' field in L3
Generation cost estimate (input/output token counts) is returned in the generate response and stored in wal_events payload

userStories.title: Pipeline Retry with Selective Story Re-execution
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to retry only the failed stories in a pipeline run instead of re-executing the entire spec so I can save time and LLM costs on partially successful runs.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/pipeline/runs/:runId/retry accepts an optional 'storyIds' array; when omitted, retries all failed stories
Retried stories create new story_result rows linked to the same run with an incremented retry count
The SSE stream emits 'story_retried' events with the story ID and attempt number
A run's status transitions from 'partial_failure' back to 'running' during retry and resolves to 'completed' or 'partial_failure' based on retry outcomes
The original failed story_result rows are preserved (not overwritten) for audit trail

userStories.title: Spec Search and Discovery Across Archive
userStories.description: As a developer, I want full-text search across all spec content including story descriptions and acceptance criteria so I can find relevant past work and avoid duplicate specifications.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/specs/archive supports a 'q' parameter that searches across spec title, story titles, story descriptions, and acceptance criteria text
Search results return matching specs with highlighted match snippets showing which field matched
Results are ranked by relevance with exact title matches weighted higher than body matches
Search supports filtering by date range (createdAfter, createdBefore) combined with text search
Search returns results within 200ms for archives containing up to 500 specs

userStories.title: Direction Stack Validation and Linting
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the direction stack to validate my YAML content against expected schemas and warn about common mistakes so I can catch configuration errors before they affect spec generation.
acceptanceCriteria: PUT /api/direction validates the content_yaml against a per-layer JSON schema and returns structured validation errors with field paths
L3 validation checks for required fields: name, type, stack (array), purpose, and key_modules (array)
GET /api/direction/preview includes a 'warnings' array flagging issues like empty layers, missing L1/L3 for the workspace, or L2 domain mismatch
Invalid YAML syntax returns a 422 with line number and column of the parse error

userStories.title: Story Dependency Visualization as DAG
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to visualize story dependencies as a directed acyclic graph so I can understand execution order and identify parallelizable stories within a spec.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/specs/:specId/graph returns a DAG representation with nodes (stories) and edges (dependsOn relationships)
The response includes a 'parallelGroups' array grouping stories that can execute concurrently based on their dependency resolution order
Circular dependencies are detected and returned as errors with the cycle path identified
The graph includes story status (pending/running/passed/failed) when viewed in the context of an active pipeline run via optional runId parameter

userStories.title: Batch Spec Generation with Brief Queue
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to queue multiple spec briefs for sequential generation so I can kick off a batch of specs and review them later without babysitting each generation.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/specs/generate/batch accepts an array of brief objects (each with brief text, workspace ID, and optional template ID) and returns a batch ID
GET /api/specs/generate/batch/:batchId returns the batch status including per-brief progress (queued/generating/completed/failed)
Briefs are processed sequentially to avoid concurrent LLM call conflicts with the Claude CLI
SSE stream emits 'batch_progress' events with batch ID, current brief index, and status
Failed briefs do not block remaining briefs in the queue; errors are captured per-brief with the LLM error message
